questions.q:
Which of the following idiom given in the alternatives has the meaning?

Barely in time, at the last moment?
questions.solution:
"Under the wire" means barely in time, at the last possible moment, e.g. He caught the train under the wire.

**Answer: Under the wire**
questions.shortcut: Recall: under the wire = just in time (the other three options are not idioms).

questions.q:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

A fate worse than death.
options: A situation or experience that is very pleasant
A situation or experience that is very unpleasant
A situation or experience that is very new
A situation or experience that is very common
questions.solution:
"A fate worse than death" refers to a situation or experience that is extremely unpleasant, so dreadful that it seems worse than death itself.

**Answer: A situation or experience that is very unpleasant**

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word from the given options.
questions.solution:
The correctly spelt word is Acquaintance (a person one knows slightly). The other options drop or misplace letters in the 'quaint' part.

**Answer: Acquaintance**

questions.q:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option “No replacement required”.

The political __imbraglio__ that arose over the new law left everyone confused.
questions.solution:
The intended word is imbroglio, meaning a confusing and complicated (often embarrassing) situation. 'Imbraglio' is misspelt.

**Answer: imbroglio**
questions.shortcut: Imbroglio = broil/confusion; the vowel after 'imbr' is 'o'.

questions.q: Choose the word that is the closest synonym to the word "guard".
questions.solution:
To guard means to protect or keep safe from harm, so the closest synonym is Defence. Attack, discard and abandon are opposite or unrelated in meaning.

**Answer: Defence**

questions.q: Choose the word that is the closest synonym to the word "expectation".
questions.solution:
Expectation is the belief that something good will happen; among the options, Hope is its closest synonym.

**Answer: Hope**

questions.q: Choose the word that is the most appropriate synonym of the word "**reliable**".
questions.solution:
Reliable means able to be depended on or trusted, so the correct synonym is Trustworthy.

**Answer: Trustworthy**
questions.shortcut: Reliable = rely + able = can be trusted.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to "departure".
questions.solution:
Departure means the act of leaving. Its opposite is Advent, which means arrival or coming into being. Exodus, exit and withdrawal are themselves synonyms of departure.

**Answer: Advent**
questions.shortcut: Advent = arrival (as in 'the advent of winter').

questions.q: Choose the word that is the antonym of Giant.
questions.solution:
Giant means extremely large, so its antonym is Tiny (extremely small). Huge, immense and enormous are synonyms of giant.

**Answer: Tiny**

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who studies insects.
questions.solution:
An entomologist is a person who studies insects (Greek entomon = insect). Zoology studies animals, botany plants and pathology diseases.

**Answer: Entomologist**
questions.shortcut: entom/o = insect, ornith/o = bird — learn these roots together.

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who studies birds.
questions.solution:
An ornithologist is a person who studies birds (Greek ornis = bird).

**Answer: Ornithologist**

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

One who takes part in an activity for pleasure and not professionally.
questions.solution:
An amateur takes part in an activity for pleasure and not professionally. Novice = beginner, apprentice = learner under a master, veteran = highly experienced person.

**Answer: Amateur**

questions.q:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.

The unprecedented decrease of direct taxes has increased the earning potential of the capitalists.
questions.solution:
The error is in part (B). After 'decrease' the correct preposition is 'in', not 'of': 'The unprecedented decrease in direct taxes has increased...'.

**Answer: (B) decrease of direct taxes has**

questions.q:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.

There is an irreparable problem of the ignition system of the car, which has to be addressed immediately.
options: of the ignition system of the car,
which has to be addressed immediately.
questions.solution:
The error is in part (C). A problem exists in something, so the phrase should be 'a problem in the ignition system', not 'of the ignition system'.

**Answer: (C) of the ignition system of the car,**

questions.q:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The teacher pulled a book ________ the cupboard.
questions.solution:
To take something out from inside a container, the phrase is 'out of': The teacher pulled a book out of the cupboard.

**Answer: out of**

questions.q:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The value of the property is not mentioned ________ the will.
questions.solution:
Something stated within a document is mentioned in it: The value of the property is not mentioned in the will.

**Answer: in**

questions.q:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option which can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: “No Improvement Required.”

Each of the representatives from the various states __have presented their reports__ on healthcare reforms.
questions.solution:
'Each of the + plural noun' takes a singular verb. Hence 'have presented' and 'were presented' are wrong; the correct phrase is 'has presented their reports'.

**Answer: has presented their reports**
questions.shortcut: Each of / Either of / Neither of + plural noun -> singular verb.

questions.q:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: “No Improvement Required.”

When scaling the Himalayas, the higher one ascends, __the lesser oxygen is available__.
questions.solution:
The 'the + comparative, the + comparative' structure must be parallel: 'the higher one ascends, the less oxygen is available'. 'Lesser' is not the correct comparative form here; 'less' is used before uncountable nouns like oxygen.

**Answer: the less oxygen is available**

questions.q:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered $1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. There was a woman on the station platform. A tall scrag of a woman wearing a little round hat with a brown feather that dropped in a draggled fringe over her eyes.

A. The toss and tumble, the hurrying threading rush of movement left her high and dry.

B. Brown button boots showed under the skirt and an end of white petticoat dabbled with mud.

C. Round her neck some indescribable little dead animal bit its own tail, its fur standing up wet and sticky like the fur of a drowned kitten.

D. She was dressed in a brown jacket and a narrow brown skirt and in her bare hands she clutched a broken down-looking leather bag-the outside pockets bulging with what looked like old torn-up envelopes.

S2. She stood as though she were part of the furniture of the station and had been there for years-an old automatic machine that nobody dreamed of slipping a coin into or even troubled to glance at to find out what once it contained-whether a drop of white rose perfume or a cachet or deux cigarettes a la reine d'Egypte.
questions.solution:
The description moves top to bottom over the woman and then to the crowd: D (brown jacket, narrow skirt, leather bag) → C (the dead little animal round her neck) → B (brown button boots and the mud-dabbled petticoat) → A (the hurrying rush of movement left her high and dry), which leads into S2 where she stands like part of the station furniture.

**Answer: DCBA**
questions.shortcut: Description order: clothes -> neck accessory -> footwear -> effect of the crowd on her.

questions.q: How does the Choice-Based Credit System (CBCS) differ from the traditional higher education system?
options: It allows students to pick courses based on their career goals.
It requires students to follow a fixed curriculum with no flexibility.
It limits students to a single discipline and discourages skill development.
It focuses solely on memorization and theoretical knowledge.
questions.solution:
Unlike the traditional fixed curriculum, CBCS gives students the freedom to choose courses (core, elective and skill-based) in line with their interests and career goals.

**Answer: It allows students to pick courses based on their career goals.**

questions.q: What factors contribute to the recognition of the Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) as a significant reform in Indian higher education?
options: It mandates uniform subject selection and does not allow learners to choose subjects based on their interests
It integrates core subjects with skill-based courses for the holistic development of the students
It limits students to traditional academic disciplines and inhibits opportunities for innovation
It overlooks international standards and concentrates solely on indigenous educational practices
questions.solution:
CBCS is regarded as a significant reform because it combines core subjects with skill-based courses, allowing holistic development of students instead of a rigid single-discipline study.

**Answer: It integrates core subjects with skill-based courses for the holistic development of the students**

questions.q: How does CBCS fit into the vision of the New Education Policy (NEP)?
options: It goes against NEP by sticking to rigid subject structures and limiting student choice
It ignores NEP recommendations and continues with outdated, one-size-fits-all curricula and discourages learners from thinking out of the box
It slows down NEP implementation by resisting reforms and discouraging skill-based education for the learners
It supports NEP reforms by encouraging flexibility, interdisciplinary learning, and global alignment in higher education
questions.solution:
CBCS fits the NEP vision because it supports flexibility, interdisciplinary learning and alignment with global standards in higher education — exactly the reforms NEP recommends.

**Answer: It supports NEP reforms by encouraging flexibility, interdisciplinary learning, and global alignment in higher education**

questions.q: Why is CBCS considered a step toward global academic standards?
options: It separates Indian education from international standards and practices.
It keeps only traditional subjects and does not focus on skill development, which makes education less competitive worldwide. This means students do not learn the skills needed for the future.
It does not accept reforms and uses old teaching methods that do not meet global standards. Because of this, students lose the chance to develop creative thinking skills.
It follows global models by giving students flexibility, interdisciplinary choices, and a credit-based system.
questions.solution:
By following global models — student flexibility, interdisciplinary choices and a credit-based structure — CBCS brings Indian higher education in line with international academic standards.

**Answer: It follows global models by giving students flexibility, interdisciplinary choices, and a credit-based system.**

questions.q: Which educational philosophy influenced the adoption of CBCS in India?
options: Traditional Indian models emphasizing rote learning
Government schemes focused solely on vocational training
International frameworks advocating flexibility and learner autonomy
Systems designed to reduce academic diversity and specialization
questions.solution:
The adoption of CBCS in India was influenced by international educational frameworks that advocate flexibility and learner autonomy rather than rote learning or rigid curricula.

**Answer: International frameworks advocating flexibility and learner autonomy**
